newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - FEB 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - FEB 27.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Surprising even brokers with its sustained and impressive performance, the Athens bourse's general price index yesterday gained another 45.9 points, increasing 3.26 percent, to close at a record 1,453.6 points. Turnover rose to an unprecedented 45.2 billion drachmas. The upward trend is being fed, brokers say, by private investors, particularly from regional areas.

--The escalation of Turkish aggressiveness is the best response to those who are pressuring for the start of unconditional talks, Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos told reporters yesterday. Referring to a Wall Street Journal report on a briefing by Turkish military officials, Pangalos said it only confirmed reports of a Turkish plan to dispute Greek sovereignty of a range of islands in the Aegean.
--Yesterday's first meeting between Prime Minister Costas Simitis and farmers who had set up the December roadblocks was fruitless.

--As teachers decided to proceed to a seventh week of their strike, reports said the prime minister was in favour of mobilising the teachers or taking the strike to court to force them back to the classrooms. The same reports said, however, that Education Minister Gerasimos Arsenis had ruled out mobilisation.

--Last night's meeting between Arsenis and the teacher's union OLME however was reported to have made some progress, with the minister compromising on the issue of new teachers but the union standing firm on financial demands.
--Turkish fighter planes infringed Greek air space near Crete yesterday as Foreign Minister Pangalos launched volleys against Greece's EU partners.
--The government's new town planning provides a 10-fold increase in charges for property owners wanting to include their land in the town planning grid.
--Conservative opposition New Democracy deputies yesterday peititioned Parliament to have the government release ailing former dictator George Papadopoulos.
--Thirteen passengers on a domestic Olympic Airways flight narrowly averted death after the plane lost its way over the Pindos mountains and landed at the wrong airport with minimal fuel.
